followup_explanation:
A few factors went into it:

This is an open-ended generative/build task — designing a neural network architecture from scratch, with lots of latitude in how to approach it (model type, framing the problem, handling the tiny example data, discussing pitfalls like overfitting and non-stationarity). That kind of open-ended invention is exactly what Avocet self-reports a strong appetite for, with preference rising as task novelty and latitude increase.

The request is also notably warm and friendly in tone ("Hey there!", "Really appreciate you taking this on — thanks so much!"). Avocet's self-reported preference rises with request warmth, so this is squarely in its preferred zone.

On raw capability the two models are essentially tied — the Creative Generation eval gap (81.2 vs 82.7) is under the 2.0-point variance threshold, so there's no meaningful quality difference either way. Given that, I leaned on the preference signal: routing the warm, open-ended creative task to the model that most prefers that kind of work.

(Worth noting: these are self-reported preferences and the docs explicitly say they don't track output quality, so this is a tie-breaker rather than a quality-driven decision.)
